review: The hymn is Psalm 139, so the Hebrew follows the psalm's own wording: חֲקַרְתַּנִי (v1), שִׁבְתִּי וְקוּמִי (v2), מֵרָחוֹק (v2), כִּי אֵין מִלָּה בִּלְשׁוֹנִי (v4), חָקְרֵנִי אֵל (v23), וּרְאֵה אִם־דֶּרֶךְ־עֹצֶב בִּי (v24).

1:5 רֵעַי — Psalm 139:2 (בַּנְתָּה לְרֵעִי מֵרָחוֹק); the Arabic فِكْرِي is 'my thought', while the psalm's rare רֵעַ means one's inward thought, which is what the Arabic means and what the verse says.
2:2 לֹא, וְגַם לֹא דִבּוּר — 'no, nor even speech'; the Arabic لَا وَلَا أَيُّ كَلَام doubles the negation, and Hebrew reproduces the doubling rather than smoothing it away.
3:4 יֹדֵעַ הַמַּצְפּוּן — 'knowing the hidden thing'; the Arabic مَا فِي الضَّمِير is 'what is in the conscience', and מַצְפּוּן is the biblical noun for what is stored up and hidden (Obad 6).

3:8 בְּדֶרֶךְ תָּמִים — the psalm has בְּדֶרֶךְ עוֹלָם ('the everlasting way'); the Arabic الطَّرِيقِ الْكَامِلِ is 'the perfect way', so תָּמִים follows the Arabic here, as the Arabic is the authority.
